
###chapter1 Encounter with Kidnappers
********
Betrayed by her fiancé and left for dead, Winnie’s survival hinges on a forbidden night with a masked stranger. Pregnant and powerless, she strikes a dangerous bargain: bear his heir, secure his protection, and destroy those who ruined her. But when her enigmatic husband’s secrets threaten her revenge, she must gamble everything to reclaim her empire.
********

On the night before her wedding, Winnie and her step-sister were kidnapped, but her fiancé only saved the sister...

The kidnapper smirked and pounced on her, tearing her clothes apart.

Winnie Anderson was a reserved and virtuous girl. She still couldn't believe it and foolishly pleaded, "Please! Can you wait a little longer? Daniel Davis promised to provide the ransom..."

The kidnapper sneered and dialed a number, shouting, "Ava Anderson, your sister is really stupid!"

Winnie's mind went blank.

Winnie heard her step-sister on the other end of the phone, mocking, "Did you really believe that your fiancé would come to save you? Let me tell you the truth, I'm pregnant with his child!"

Winnie's face turned pale as she asked, "When did you two get together?"

"He has always loved me. Being with you was just a means to help him start a company! Now that he's the CEO, guess why you were kidnapped?"

Winnie felt her limbs go cold and shook her head repeatedly. "I don't believe it, let Daniel tell me himself!"

"He's in my bed. I couldn't resist him even when I got pregnant."

A heartless voice came from the phone, "Winnie, you're of no use anymore. Have a safe journey!" Daniel says indifferently.

Boom! Realization hit Winnie as her face began to turn extremely pale. Eight years of love turned out to be just a deceitful manipulation. He wanted her dead for the sake of taking over the company! Tears started to stream down Winnie's face uncontrollably. 

Ava sneered, "He even wanted to keep your body intact, so I'll make sure you die a horrible death. Have fun with them first, and then they'll feed you to the wolves!"

"Ava, I've always treated you like a sister. Why are you doing this to me? Our parents won't forgive you!"

"Do you really think our parents truly love you?" Ava sneers.

Winnie freezes. What does she mean by that? 

However, before she can ponder further, the kidnapper begins to drag her deep into the mountains!

They press down on her with wicked smiles. 

Winnie trembles in fear, unwilling to accept it!

Is she really going to be played to death by Daniel and Ava's scheme, by these people?

No way!

Suddenly, she notices a black car parked down the hill, right by the roadside in the darkness. The car door seems to be open strangely, and there's a man seated in the backseat. His tall silhouette is blurred, but the atmosphere feels different, clearly tense and suppressed.

Summoning all her strength, she forcefully breaks free from the kidnapper, rolls down the mountain, and rushes toward the car.

Desperately pleading, she asks, "Sir, can you let me in? Could I get in the car to hide for a while?"

"Go away," the man with cold, narrowed eyes breathed heavily, warning. 

Meanwhile, the kidnappers were catching up from behind!

"Someone is after me, sir, please!" Winnie clung to his thigh out of desperation and climbed up, closing the car door behind her.

Her trembling body kept rubbing against the man's trousers unconsciously.

In the darkness, his bloodthirsty eyes suddenly opened, and the man growled, "Aren't you getting down?"

"I can't get down!" She hurriedly tried to climb to the front to drive.

The man smirked coldly, "Then don't regret it!" As he said that, the man pulled her back.

Winnie was dumbfounded, she stared with wide eyes and cried. 

Gradually, darkness overwhelmed her. 

She didn't know how long had passed until she slowly regained consciousness...

The man was still asleep, and it wasn't yet dawn. 

Winnie picked up her clothes and quickly escaped from the car. That night, she escaped from the kidnappers but lost the most precious thing! And to a stranger nonetheless.

Winnie wiped the corners of her eyes sorrowfully, not daring to stay or turn back to look at the man in the car.

-

Ten days later, Winnie, barely alive, finally returned to Lymington and the Anderson family.

She had no money when she fled from the car, and along the way, she endured hunger and cold, only left with half of her life.

Winnie clenched her fists. In these ten days, she hadn't seen any news of her father searching for her.

Ava said that their father didn't love her at all. And recalling the unfair treatment she had received since childhood... Winnie bit her lip tightly.

She didn't believe it. She came back risking her life to question everything.

Winnie walked coldly into the back door of the Anderson family home and before she even stepped into the house, she heard an argument in the living room.

"She's dead, and we haven't found the body. How can we be at ease?" Her stepmother, Sophia Anderson, sounded worried.

Ava's tone was sinister as she said, "Don't worry about that; we only care about the money she left behind."

"Aren't you being too harsh?" came her father Matthew Anderson's indifferent voice.

Trembling, Winnie slipped and fell to the ground. Her expressionless face felt bone-chillingly cold. She had fantasized about her father's guilt and concern for her safety, and about her stepmother and Ava's constant worry.

But she never expected that they only thought about exploiting her value after her death.

"What's harsh, my dear? You were the one who wanted to groom Winnie for the sake of protecting Ava! 

"Besides, think about how we treated her mother back then. If Winnie is still alive and discovers your secret..."

"Enough! If she's not dead, I'll make sure she dies right here, today!" Matthew Anderson's voice sounded far from being compassionate as a father. 

"Next, let's smear her reputation. Ava and Daniel will take over her company. The things left by her grandfather will belong to me," her father continued.

"They're as good as gone, as well as her uncle. They'll be dealt with sooner or later..."

'It seems hell is empty, and all the devils are here,' Winnie thought bitterly to herself as she bit her lip, restraining herself from rushing in and fighting desperately. 

Terror and overwhelming anger caused intense pain in her abdomen. She understood now that there was something behind her mother's death, a hidden motive, and even more so, her own origins were suspicious.

She couldn't die here!

Winnie's heart was wrenching. Holding her stomach, she ran out and hailed a taxi, saying, "Take me to the hospital..."

"On tonight's broadcast, the Anderson family... Winnie Anderson... Suspected of having multiple affairs. She was killed by a lover in the mountains. Her family is devastated and desperately searching for her body..." The radio in the car was playing.

Winnie fell silent for a moment. A cold smile played on her lips. 

She had long awaited news of her family searching for her. But they twisted the truth to pour dirt on her 'death,' didn't they? They reversed right and wrong! It was all so that the awful cheating couple, Daniel and Ava, could rightfully take everything from her! 

A hatred so fierce began to stir within her. She had to keep herself alive. She wanted revenge!

"Miss Anderson?!" The driver shouted as he saw her fainting. "Why is this girl so badly injured?"

Winnie faintly heard the doctor rushing over...

When she woke up again, Winnie found a needle in the back of her hand. 

The doctor came over with a test result and was surprised. "Miss Anderson, your HCG levels are high. This proves that not only are you injured, but you are also pregnant!"

Winnie stiffened, as if struck by lightning. "Doctor...what did you say?"

"It's an early pregnancy of less than two weeks. Isn't your boyfriend here with you?"

Winnie's cherry lips turned pale. It had to be the rapist from ten days ago in the dark night! Why was she so unlucky to end up pregnant?

Seeing her reaction, the doctor seemed to have understood what happened. "Do you want to have an abortion? I can help you make an appointment for the procedure..."

"No one is allowed to touch my baby!" 

Suddenly, a group of people stormed into the emergency room.

The leader was an impeccably dressed man, who directly kicked the doctor out.

He turned and politely nodded at Winnie, saying, "Miss Anderson, you're pregnant, right? Please come with us."

Winnie felt uneasy. "Who are you?"

"We represent the father of the child you are carrying. Please come with us!"


###chapter 2 The Father of the Child Appears

Winnie froze. Her face turned pale, and her heart was pounding. She realized she was completely clueless about the man's height or appearance!

Her intention was merely to seek help, but instead, she found herself angry and humiliated.

The man quickly ushered her into the car.

Winnie didn't resist and silently complied; she had nowhere else to go. 

In the crowded hospital, she, Lymington's top debutante, sensed vulnerability. She was undeniably stepping into a precarious situation, where her own family seemed poised for her demise!

With clasped hands, Winnie discreetly observed the elegant Bentley. 

The man received a phone call and spoke with respect, "Yes, Madam, Miss Anderson is with us now."
  
"Don't get too excited. Your little grandchildren haven't even gestated yet." On the other end of the phone, a man was coaxing the elderly woman.
  
The car quickly arrived at a discreet wealthy villa on the mountainside. As Winnie stepped out of the car, two maids awaited at the door to welcome her.
  
"This is Grace and Taylor. They will take care of you for ten months until you give birth." the man said.
  
Winnie was taken aback, realizing that she had been deceived. Her eyes turned cold and she said, "He raped me and now wants to imprison me to have his child? Bring that scoundrel to see me."
  
"Mr. Rodriguez is not a scoundrel. He was ambushed that day, otherwise you wouldn't have had a chance."

Despite her anger, Winnie was forced into the house, weakened but resolute. She initiated a hunger strike and the servants had no choice but to summon their master. 

In the evening, Taylor finally brought the news, "Mr. Rodriguez will see you in the evening." 

Winnie clenched her hand secretly, feeling a mix of anger and curiosity about the man.

Late at night, Winnie hid in his bedroom and heard an engine downstairs. A hushed conversation followed, and her door slowly creaked open.

Winnie's heart raced as she picked up a vase, holding her breath in anticipation. The door opened, revealing an unusually tall shadow. A man exuded an intimidating presence, making the room feel colder.

Before she could react, Winnie saw the gentleman knock at the door, and a pair of remarkable long legs entered. Panicking, she raised the vase in anger.

The man extinguished the cigarette in his hand, his slender fingers hanging down. He coldly reminded her, "Before attacking me, take care of yourself. Don't stumble!"

Confused, Winnie locked eyes with him. 

His voice was elegant, deep, and tough. The man before her appeared gentle, reserved, and even polite, but also distant and cold-a master of mature control. It was challenging to reconcile these contrasting aspects.

As he turned, Winnie noticed him wearing a silver half-mask.

She couldn't discern his features, but she could tell his nose had a prominent bridge, his profile was sharp, and his jawline was impeccably defined.

He held onto Winnie's vase, his gaze fixed on her. "I apologize if I hurt you that day. It's the only apology I can offer."

Winnie was stupefied, her face flushing. His towering figure loomed over her, casting an oppressive gaze as he mocked, "I don't care about your intentions for getting into my car, though I suspect you had planned on getting pregnant to have my mother find you..."

"You misunderstand!" Winnie bit her lip. 

The man spoke with condescension. "My mother has only a year left to live. To fulfill her wishes, I agree to marry you. If you have a baby and leave after a year, I'll compensate you!" His words sounded more like commands than negotiations.

Winnie looked slightly annoyed. "Why should I promise you to be used as a tool for having children and deceiving people?" 

In response, he turned on the TV, a hint of playfulness in his eyes.

Winnie read the news on the screen. "Winnie Anderson's father Matthew confirmed that Winnie had an affair and was killed! The Anderson family plans to hold the funeral tomorrow afternoon. According to her will, her company, Triton Jewelry., will be taken over by Daniel, and the enormous wealth left by her grandfather will be inherited by Ava. The Anderson family is mourning deeply"

Winnie's face turned pale with hatred and she trembled. They were so eager to bury her, they had even crafted a flawless forgery of her will!

"The Anderson family treated you like this; don't you want revenge?" 

"I do!" Winnie gritted her teeth. She had placed so much trust in this false sense of family. Her father had entrusted her with taking care of Ava, and Daniel had asked her to support Ava, promising to marry her. So, she had given her all, unknowingly creating a perfect wedding dress for others!

"You're a 'dead' person. You don't even have a place to hide. Do you have a choice?" The man's ink-black eyes bore into hers as he negotiated fiercely. He handed over an agreement and elegantly placed it down.

Winnie took a deep breath, tears welling up in her almond eyes. She lowered her head and whispered, "No. I need your protection."

He stood proudly. 

"My protection depends on your sincerity to cooperate. We will sign a marriage contract with three clauses: no interference, no betrayal, and no attempt to fall in love with me." 

How narcissistic. Nevertheless, Winnie picked up the pen and slowly signed her name. 

The man stood up and said tersely, "We'll register our marriage tomorrow!" 

She nodded and hesitated before asking with a furrowed brow, "Do I have to give birth to this child?" 

The man turned his head, his emotions were hard to discern, "You don't want to?" Winnie bit her lip. She and him were not familiar at all... and the child was conceived in that situation. 

He walked slowly toward her, pinched her chin to raise her face and gazed upon her exquisite beauty-tempting and charming, still young at the age of 23, with soft and tender red lips. 

The man's voice was low, "Although there are some things, I am willing to take care of..."

Winnie hesitated, not understanding his words. 

He smirked, his tone serious as he continued, "I respect life, so give birth to it!" 

His dominance struck Winnie. She suddenly grasped the meaning behind his offer to "take care of" things, and her face inexplicably blushed.

The man walked coldly to the door, but before opening it, an excited woman's voice echoed outside. "You brat, I'll show you what death looks like if you dare to come out tonight!" 

The door was locked!

Winnie was somewhat confused, "Who is that outside the door?" 

"My mom." His face darkened. He returned and pulled her to the edge of the bed, his voice deep and charming, "Will you cooperate?" 

"Cooperate with what?" 

"Let's act out the wedding night."

Winnie looked at his mature ink-like eyes, seemingly capable of devouring people, and suddenly understood his meaning. Her face turned crimson. "But... I don't know how."

He frowned and abruptly pressed her forcefully against the headboard, his large hand tugging at her clothing. 

"Hey! What are you doing?" 

"Now do you understand?" He raised an eyebrow with an evil smirk. 

Outside the door, there was an immediate murmur of joy, "Thank goodness, the brat has finally grown some sense!"

Awkwardness enveloped Winnie as she found herself pinned down, her fragrant shoulder exposed, its skin as smooth as milk. The man's gaze swept over her, darkening slightly as he caught a whiff of a sweet scent...

In the sudden closeness, Winnie could only sense his solid and powerful muscles. Her cheeks blazed red, sensing the danger, and she desperately wished for him to leave quickly. In an attempt to convey her discomfort, she deliberately let out an "ah" in a miserable cry.

"Watch it, you brat! My daughter-in-law is pregnant with my grandchild!" 

The man lowered his head, his gaze fixed on the blushing woman. "Are you trying to get back at me?"

Winnie rolled her apricot eyes. "Can we stop now?" 

His thin lips lightly curled. He decided not to give her any more trouble. He got up and released her.

The forbidding and cold air dissipated as the man walked over to the sofa and sat down. He casually removed his tie and his broad shoulders, slim waist, and long legs made him exude nobility and aloofness. This man indeed had the capital to be narcissistic! 

Winnie huddled at the head of the bed, glancing at the door anxiously. She nervously asked, "Are we sleeping together tonight?" 

"Do you want to?" He picked up a magazine, glancing at her with his black eyes. 

Then, his pleasant voice hummed with sarcasm, "Do you think I would lower myself to touch a young pregnant woman?"

His tone, mocking and serious, referred to her as a pregnant woman. Winnie felt a twinge of annoyance.

Was he really that much older than her? She wondered.

Gazing at his silver mask, curiosity filled her. Was it because he was hideous or had scars that he didn't want to show? 

He sat there motionless, only switching off the lights when Winnie finished changing and climbed into bed.

Winnie cautiously and tentatively asked, "Sir, you seem to know everything about me. So, may I ask, how old are you and what's your name?" 

There was a prolonged silence, and he ignored her, as though the question had fallen on deaf ears.

###chapter 3 A case of mysophobia

This man was distant and inscrutable. He was very difficult to get along with. The superiority and mystery he carried were attributes Winnie, hailing from a prestigious family herself, recognized as qualities reserved for the elite.

"My name is Lawrence," the man whispered in a low tone as she was almost asleep.

The next morning, after Winnie got up and had breakfast, she noticed Melissa Clark across from her, looking at her with a smile.

"Winnie, I think you two are a perfect match. You should take good care of yourself. Come on and have more caviar." Melissa encouraged before shifting her focus.

Winnie almost choked on her food at the madam's statement. Despite her lively demeanor, one would never guess she had only a year to live, given her pale complexion.

Winnie's gaze drifted to the handsome figure, Lawrence Rodriguez, in a white shirt and black suit at the far end of the dining table. He still wore a silver half-mask, showcasing a high, straight nose and beautiful thin lips. 

However, his expression remained cold, evidently accustomed to his mother's lack of seriousness.

The servants and Melissa showed no different reaction to his mask.

This only fueled Winnie's confusion. Who exactly was he? His identity remained shrouded in mystery.

At this moment, Taylor descended from upstairs with a blanket and asked quietly, "Madam, the blanket is clean. Shall I put it away?"

Winnie glanced over, not understanding his meaning.

Melissa noticed her curiosity and explained with a smile, "This is a festive blanket, used on wedding nights. Even the servants don't understand the rules and gave it to you..."

"Your thinking is too closed-minded!" Lawrence interjected unhappily.

Approaching Winnie's table to grab some jam, he paused with his long legs and raised an eyebrow, "She was a virgin, and I know it." The insinuation was clear-first-time sexual intercourse might result in bleeding.

"Am I right?" Somewhat uncertain, he leaned closer to Winnie's ear and asked her.

Winnie's snow-white ears turned red; how could she respond to this?

Especially since he didn't leave and his cool masculine breath carried pressure, emanating a pleasant scent that stirred her skin.

Afraid that he might say even more outrageous things, she could only scoop up a spoonful of soup angrily and stuff it into his mouth, "Please eat, and speak less."

"Mrs. Rodriguez... Mr. Rodriguez has a severe case of mysophobia!" Taylor was frightened.

However, Lawrence just stared at Winnie and surprisingly swallowed the spoonful of soup, his thin lips faintly curling as he walked away.

The more composed he was, the more Winnie blushed. Looking at the spoon he had eaten from, she didn't know whether she should pick it up or not!

Melissa smirked and handed her the spoon, "Winnie, you should eat quickly. It's like having a sweet indirect kiss... Hm? What happened to your palm, child?"

She suddenly grabbed Winnie's right hand.

Winnie lowered her head. A frosty gaze appeared in her eyes. Memories of the day Ava stepped on her palm during the kidnapping resurfaced. If she hadn't known medicine and collected herbs while escaping, her hand would have been useless long ago!

Ava was jealous of her gifted hands!

"Why didn't you say anything last night?" the man said coldly, furrowing his brow slightly. "Taylor, go call the doctor," he ordered sternly.

When the family doctor arrived, Winnie was shocked. Wasn't he the most famous doctor in Lymington? The Anderson family had tried numerous times to get him to visit, but they failed every time, and yet, it seemed he was a resident in this villa?

Who in the world was Lawrence? Winnie wondered.

"Ah!" Winnie winced in pain from the medicine as it was applied.

This caught Lawrence's attention, and he put down the newspaper, immediately feeling uneasy.  Crossing his long legs, he saw the horrifying scars on her small hand, remembering her fingers as soft and white that night, on his body...

He gulped, then raised an eyebrow as he stood up, commanding the doctor, "Don't leave her hand with scars!"

The doctor trembled nervously under Lawrence's instruction.

Melissa smiled and whispered to Winnie, "Seems like he really cherishes your hands. Oh, what a naughty boy!"

Winnie, with her face flushed red, was forced to understand. She had never met such an open-minded woman before. As she blushed, the man ignored her, only casting a serious glance her way every once in a while.

Melissa immediately scoffed in his direction.

...

After breakfast, Winnie and Lawrence were pushed out of the house by Melissa, "Go and get your marriage license! I won't feel at ease until you do!"

Outside, the Bentley was already parked at the door. Lawrence, being a gentleman opened the car door while Winnie awkwardly got in.

The assistant handed him a laptop as he sat in front, and he didn't say another word.

Winnie wanted to sneak a peek at his information from the laptop, but she didn't dare. 

Winnie sat in the back seat and for the first time that morning had a chance to take in the day. It was a cool day, and not particularly hot even though the sun was out.

Winnie began to ponder the events of the last two days, and she was lost in her thoughts for the rest of the drive.

Soon, they arrived at City Hall.

There weren't many people getting their marriage licenses on this day, so the process should be relatively simple Winnie thought. But as soon as Winnie got out of the car, she froze as though struck by horror she saw two familiar figures!

Daniel and Ava!

###chapter 4 The bitch couple, she’s back
On the eleventh day after they cruelly "killed" her in the kidnapping scheme, they secretly came to get their marriage license.

What a coincidence!

Winnie stood there fiercely, overwhelmed by suffocating pain, deep-seated hatred that pierced her heart, and a chill bursting from her eyes.

All the past mockery was like a dagger piercing through her heart!

"Winnie, I'll definitely marry you. You'll be Mrs. Davis right away."

"Winnie, you're a genius. Help Ava with the designs again. She must win the jewelry competition!"

"We'll get our license after the wedding, don't worry, I won't betray you."

But after the wedding, He simply wanted her dead!

The man standing tall beside her released her clenched fist and asked in a cold tone, "Do you need a few minutes?"

Winnie pressed her pale lips together and shook her head.

The polite staff escorted them in.

It only took about two minutes to obtain the documents. Winnie glanced at the cold man working diligently in his chair, dominant, indifferent, and perfunctory.

Did she just enter a lonely marriage? It seemed like getting the license was only a way to satisfy his mother.

He knew nothing about her, and she didn't know who she had just married.

At that moment, Winnie suddenly saw Daniel and Ava walking into another office room from outside, with Ava carrying a bag and heading to the restroom.

She smirked, her cherry lips curling, and said to Lawrence, "I need to take care of something."

The assistant, Bryan, looked at the cold and slender back of Winnie, then asked his boss with a lowered voice, "Mr. Rodriguez?"

Lawrence's gaze didn't leave his work, only furrowing his brows, "Go with her, and protect her."

In the restroom, Winnie retrieved a broken lipstick and water from her bag, using them to smear a piece of paper. She then discreetly placed it inside one of the cubicles, offering a cold smile before leaving.

Outside City Hall, Winnie asked the driver to stop the car for a moment.

After waiting quietly for a few seconds, a panicked and delicate figure tumbled down the steps, screaming without caring about her image, "Daniel!"

Daniel ran toward her, finding Ava with a flushed face.

Trembling, Ava pulled out a bloodstained piece of paper.

"Look... a birthday greeting in blood, matching the deceased, with Winnie's name on it! It just appeared in my bag. Is it Winnie? Has she returned to claim our lives?!"

Scared by the bloody paper, Daniel took two steps back, furrowing his brow as he supported Ava. "Nonsense. She's already dead! Stay calm, and let's not attract the paparazzi."

"Daniel, I'm so scared..." Ava's eyes darkened, her face pale.

Looking at the couple huddled together and scanning their surroundings, Winnie coldly smirked and snapped a photo with her phone. The wound in her hand throbbed. The excruciating pain reminded her of her stepmother's words, and her pupils dilated.

"What's harsh, my dear? You were the one who wanted to groom Winnie for the sake of protecting Ava!"

The painful truth cut deep, and from now on, she vowed to become Ava's catastrophe!

Winnie glanced at the afternoon funeral news, her lips curling into a cold smile. The appetizers were served; the main event would soon follow. 

With deep-seated vengeance brewing within, she would settle everything and take back what was rightfully hers.

She cradled her hand, which was spasming in pain, and said, "Mr. Rodriguez, you can drive now."

Suddenly, her pale hand was grabbed by a larger hand, and the man beside her momentarily shifted his attention from work, asking about her hand, "Does it hurt?"

His deep, low voice made Winnie freeze in an instant. Almost at that moment, the tears she had been holding back were about to stream down her face. 

"Don't cry! Let me massage it for you." Lawrence frowned and gave it a light rub. There was no emotion on his profile, just a cool and solid presence.

Winnie stared blankly at this nobleman, and he asserted, "I don't care what you're planning to do, just promise me that our baby will be safe!"

"I promise!" It was a transaction from the beginning, and Winnie didn't expect him to help her seek revenge, especially since he doubted her true intentions.

But she needed a place to stay, and this marriage was her best move.

"Drop her off," He said as he continued working on his laptop, obviously busy. He did not state any destination.

Winnie gazed at his upright figure in a suit and told the driver, "Please take me to Sunset Funeral Parlor!"

Meanwhile, in the VIP lounge of the funeral home, Sophia scoffed as she tore up the bloody paper. "It's just a prank with lipstick. Don't be frightened!"

Ava was still a bit traumatized. "But no one else knows about the ghost marriage we arranged for her!"

Sophia disdainfully said, "Even if everyone in her company has sided with us, she will still have one or two rotten friends. It's just a petty prank."

"Hmph, the funeral is about to begin. Your father will publicly announce that all her inheritance rights belong to you, and there will no longer be a person called Winnie in this world!"

"She's dead. There's no way she can come back." Matthew was firm.

Hearing that, Ava regained her composure, a victorious smugness appearing on her face.

At two o'clock in the afternoon, many people came to attend the funeral.

The Anderson family was a well-known aristocratic family in Lymington. Particularly, the sensational Winnie Anderson had made a name for herself by launching her business at the tender age of 18, showcasing both talent and remarkable beauty.

Her demise was now a shocking reality, and the disgraceful manner of her death had ignited a considerable commotion.

Squinting her eyes, Winnie stood on the side of the road, making a public phone call. Despite having nothing now, she still recalled some familiar media contacts.

Concealing the blood plasma purchased by the driver, she donned sunglasses and removed the gauze from her palm as she entered the funeral home.

A cold smile played on her lips-she was back!

The dirge played as Winnie glimpsed at the empty coffin in the middle.

"The once glorious debutante, who would have thought it would end like this," someone whispered. 

"Did you not see the news? She was murdered by her lover! Despite her innocent appearance, it's long been rumored that she was promiscuous and got ahead in business by sleeping around. She cheated on Daniel and bullied her step-sister!" 

"That's right, I work at Triton Jewelry and have seen Winnie Anderson sleep with the male shareholders. She also constantly tormented Ava Anderson." 

"Enough of your gossip," Ava says tearfully, "I am saddened by Winnie's death. I can forgive her for taking credit for my designs"

"She was so arrogant and constantly humiliated Ava. It's all for the better now that that bitch is dead," another person angrily remarked. 

Winnie leaned against a corner, tightly clenching her fist with a cold smile. 

"Silence, all of you!" demanded an angry female voice, "Ava, you're shamelessly biting the hand that fed you. It's you who stole Winnie's design and spread false rumors about her even after her death. Your heart is damned!" 

Winnie stiffened as Olivia, her best friend, appeared at the funeral.

Ava signaled to an employee who immediately grabbed Olivia. "You and Winnie were birds of a feather. How dare you spread rumors about me here? Drag her out!"

Olivia Smith was quickly taken down despite her feeble resistance. But she could only look at the memorial platform and sob, "Winnie, I know you were wrongfully accused"

Winnie's eyes twitched with bitterness as she clenched her fist tightly. She would turn the tables; she silently promised Olivia.

The memorial service began, and Winnie, with disheveled hair, took advantage of the lack of attention and quickly slipped into the wreaths.

Matthew stood on the main podium, tears streaming down his face. "My dear daughter has died, but those who are still alive must continue. According to Winnie's will, she voluntarily bequeathed all of her company assets to Ava"

Suddenly, the coffin moved! 

The whole room fell silent. Matthew looked up, and the coffin was right beside him on the left. Bloody things started appearing from the flower-covered coffin.

"What is that? It's... a hand!" 

"But, wasn't Winnie's body not found?"

###chapter 5 The Husband’s Unknown name
 
The atmosphere suddenly became horrifying! Just then, a bloody figure crawled out of the coffin and cried out in anguish, "Dad, I'm in so much pain! Am I already dead?"

Matthew mechanically looked up, terrified, and fell to the ground! The bloody corpse crawled out of the coffin and crawled in front of Sophia. "Sophia, I'm in so much pain. Ava stomped on the palm of my hand."

"Ava, you let the kidnappers beat me up so badly."

"Ah! Ah! Ah!" Sophia and Ava screamed and fell to the ground. The three of them were pale from shock.

Ava, holding her head and shouting incoherently, said, "Mom, we sent her to hell. She shouldn't be able to come back! How did her ghost find us? No, don't come near me!"

Her words revealed an important piece of information. Winnie coldly smirked as she slowly stood up. The crowd was visibly terrified, their faces turned pale. A few of them raised their eyes and saw Winnie moving freely. Trembling, they asked, "Miss Anderson, are you not dead?"

"No!" Winnie walked over, stepped on Ava's hand, and looked down with a chilling smile.

"But what's strange is that my family all thought I was dead and even wanted to send me to hell."
